# std.strings

String algorithms. They only compare elements, so they work on a `Str` (ASCII bytes) and on any `List<T>` alike. Positions are 0-based.

In prelude (no `use` needed): `Palindromes`, `RollingHash`, `SuffixArray`, `borders`, `common_prefix_len`, `common_suffix_len`, `digit`, `ends_with`, `find_all`, `lower`, `lyndon_factorization`, `manacher`, `min_rotation`, `overlap`, `period`, `prefix_function`, `repeat`, `starts_with`, `upper`, `z_function`.

## `struct KmpAutomaton<A>`

\(O(\lvert \mathit{pat} \rvert \cdot \lvert A \rvert)\).

Fields: `alpha: Count`, `goto: List<Count>`, `pi: List<Count>`.

- `fn new<S: Seq>(pat: S) -> KmpAutomaton<A>` — \(O(\lvert \mathit{pat} \rvert \cdot \lvert A \rvert)\); The KMP automaton of `pat` over the alphabet domain `A`: one state per matched prefix length `0..=pat.len`, with a full transition table.; traps: when an element of `pat` is not in `A`
- `@get fn len(self) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); The number of states, `pat.len + 1`; the states are `0..=pat.len` and `pat.len` means a full match.
- `fn step(self, state: Int, a: A) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); The matched prefix length after reading `a` in `state`.; traps: when `state` is outside `0..self.len`
- `fn link(self, state: Int) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); The failure link of `state`: the length of the longest proper border of `pat[..state]`, and `0` at state `0`.; traps: when `state` is outside `0..self.len`
- `fn find_all<S: Seq>(self, text: S) -> yields Int` — \(O(\lvert \mathit{text} \rvert)\); The start position (0-based, counted in `text`'s iteration order) of every occurrence of `pat` in `text`, overlapping ones included.; traps: when an element of `text` is not in `A`

## `struct Palindromes(pub odd: List<Int>, even: List<Int>, first: Int = 0)`

\(O(n)\) space, \(O(1)\) queries.

- `@get fn len(self) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); The length of the sequence the radii were computed for.
- `@get fn is_empty(self) -> Bool` — \(O(1)\); True when the sequence the radii were computed for is empty.
- `fn longest_at<K>(self, i: K) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); The length of the longest odd-length palindrome centred on the element at key `i` of the sequence the radii were computed for, so a slice is asked in its own keys (R04b.5.6).; traps: when `i` is not one of the sequence's keys
- `fn longest_between(self, i: Int) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); The length of the longest even-length palindrome centred on the cut `i` (between positions `i - 1` and `i`), `2 * even[i]`; `0` at the cuts `0` and `self.len`.; traps: when `i` is outside `0..=self.len`
- `fn is_palindrome<R>(self, r: R) -> Bool` — \(O(1)\); True when the positions `r` (`l..r`, `l..=r`, or a `Range<D>`) of the original sequence form a palindrome: `p.is_palindrome(l..r) == is_palindrome(s[l..r])`.; traps: when `r` reaches outside `0..=self.len`
- `fn count(self) -> Int` — \(O(n)\); The number of non-empty palindromic substrings, each occurrence counted: `sum(odd) + sum(even)`.
- `fn longest(self) -> (l: Int, r: Int)` — \(O(n)\); The half-open range `(l, r)` of a longest palindromic substring.

## `struct SuffixArray<T: Ord>`

\(O(n)\) SA-IS + Kasai LCP (\(O(n \log n)\) with RMQ).

Fields: `rank: List<Int>`, `rmq: List<Int>`, `bits: Int`, `dcum: List<Int>`, `src: List<T>`.

- `fn new<S: Indexed<K, T>, K>(s: S) -> SuffixArray<T>` — \(O(n)\) for `Str` and small integer alphabets, \(O(n \log n)\) otherwise; The suffix array of `s` with its inverse and LCP array: `sa[r]` is the start of the suffix of rank `r`, `rank[sa[r]] == r`, and `lcp[r]` is the LCP of the suffixes of ranks `r` and `r + 1`.
- `@get fn len(self) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); The length `n` of the sequence the suffix array was built over.
- `@get fn is_empty(self) -> Bool` — \(O(1)\); True when the suffix array was built over an empty sequence.
- `fn lcp_between(self, i: Int, j: Int) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); The length of the longest common prefix of the suffixes starting at `i` and `j`.; traps: when `i` or `j` is outside `0..=self.len`
- `fn rank_range<P: Indexed<J, T>, J>(self, pat: P) -> Range<Int>` — \(O(\lvert \mathit{pat} \rvert \log n)\); The ranks `lo..hi` of the suffixes that start with `pat`.
- `fn find_all<P: Indexed<J, T>, J>(self, pat: P) -> yields Int` — \(O(\lvert \mathit{pat} \rvert \log n + \mathit{occurrences})\); The start of every occurrence of `pat`, read off `sa` over `rank_range(pat)`.
- `fn count<P: Indexed<J, T>, J>(self, pat: P) -> Int` — \(O(\lvert \mathit{pat} \rvert \log n)\); The number of occurrences of `pat`, overlapping ones included: `rank_range(pat).len`.
- `fn lcp_range(self, i: Int, len: Int) -> Range<Int>` — \(O(\log n)\); The ranks `lo..hi` of the suffixes whose LCP with the suffix at `i` is at least `len`; always contains `rank[i]`.; traps: when `i` is outside `0..n` or `len` outside `0..=n - i`
- `fn compare(self, l1: Int, r1: Int, l2: Int, r2: Int) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); The lexicographic comparison of `s[l1..r1]` and `s[l2..r2]`: `-1`, `0` or `1`.; traps: when a range is not within `0..=n` or has its end before its start
- `fn distinct(self) -> Int` — \(O(n)\); The number of distinct non-empty substrings: `n * (n + 1) / 2 - sum(lcp)`.
- `fn lcp_of_ranks(self, r: Range<Int>) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); The longest prefix common to every suffix with rank in `r`: the minimum of `lcp[j]` for `j in r.start..r.end - 1`, or the suffix's own length when `r` holds one rank.; traps: when `r` is empty or reaches outside `0..n`
- `fn split(self, r: Range<Int>) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); Where the rank range `r` splits in the suffix tree: the `k` in `r.start + 1..r.end` whose adjacent LCP `lcp[k - 1]` equals `lcp_of_ranks(r)`, so `r.start..k` and `k..r.end` are the first child and the rest.; traps: when `r.len < 2` or `r` reaches outside `0..n`
- `fn kth_distinct(self, k: Int) -> ?Range<Int>` — \(O(\log n)\); The `k`-th (0-based) lexicographically smallest distinct non-empty substring, as the positions `l..r` of one occurrence, or `None` when `k >= distinct()`.; traps: when `k < 0`

## `struct RollingHash`

\(O(n)\) build, \(O(1)\) slice hash.

Fields: `p1: List<Int>`, `p2: List<Int>`, `pow1: List<Int>`, `pow2: List<Int>`.

- `fn new<S: Seq>(seq: S, bases: ?(Int, Int) = None) -> RollingHash` — \(O(n)\); A double-modulus polynomial rolling hash of `seq`; call it as `RollingHash(seq)`.; traps: when a given base is outside `2..M`
- `fn push<T: Hashable>(mut self, x: T)` — \(O(1)\) amortized; Appends `x` to the end of the hashed sequence.
- `fn pop(mut self)` — \(O(1)\); Removes the last element of the hashed sequence.; traps: when the hash is empty
- `fn hash_of<S: Seq>(self, seq: S) -> HashVal` — \(O(\lvert \mathit{seq} \rvert)\); The hash `seq` would have under `self`'s bases, without building a `RollingHash` of it; compare it with any slice of `self`.
- `fn concat(self, parts: List<(hash: HashVal, len: Int)>) -> HashVal` — \(O(\lvert \mathit{parts} \rvert)\) amortized; The hash of the concatenation of `parts`, each given as its hash and length, under `self`'s bases; `combine` folded left to right.; traps: when a `len` is negative
- `@get fn len(self) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); The number of elements hashed.
- `@get fn is_empty(self) -> Bool` — \(O(1)\); True when no elements are hashed.
- `@get fn all(self) -> HashVal` — \(O(1)\); The hash of the whole sequence, `self.get(0..self.len)`.
- `fn slice(self, l: Int, r: Int) -> HashVal` — \(O(1)\); The hash of the half-open slice `l..r` (0-based); `HashVal(0, 0)` when `l == r`.; traps: when `l > r`, `l < 0` or `r > self.len`
- `fn get<R>(self, r: R) -> HashVal` — \(O(1)\); The hash of a range of positions: `l..r`, `l..=r`, `..k`, `k..`, or a `Range<D>` when the hash was built over a `[D]T`.; traps: when the range reaches outside the hashed sequence
- `fn combine(self, a: HashVal, b: HashVal, b_len: Int) -> HashVal` — \(O(1)\) when `b_len <= len`, else \(O(\log b_len)\); The hash of `a`'s sequence followed by `b`'s, where `b` has length `b_len`: `a * base^b_len + b` per modulus.; traps: when `b_len < 0`
- `fn lcp(self, a: Int, b: Int, of: ?RollingHash = None) -> Int` — \(O(\log n)\); The length of the longest common prefix of the suffixes at `a` and `b`, by binary search on hashes (so it can be wrong on a collision); `of: other` puts `b` in `other`, built with the same bases.; traps: when `a` is outside `0..=self.len`, `b` outside `0..=` the len of `of` (or `self`), or
- `fn lcs(self, a: Int, b: Int) -> Int` — \(O(\log n)\); The length of the longest common suffix of the prefixes `s[..a]` and `s[..b]`, by binary search on hashes.; traps: when `a` or `b` is outside `0..=self.len`

\(O(n)\) build, \(O(1)\) query.

- `fn new<S: Seq>(seq: S, base: ?U64 = None) -> RollingHash61` — \(O(n)\); A single-modulus polynomial rolling hash of `seq` modulo the Mersenne prime `2^61 - 1`; call it as `RollingHash61(seq)`.; traps: when a given base is outside `2..2^61 - 1`
- `@get fn len(self) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); The number of elements hashed.
- `@get fn is_empty(self) -> Bool` — \(O(1)\); True when no elements are hashed.
- `@get fn all(self) -> Hash61` — \(O(1)\); The hash of the whole sequence, `self.get(0..self.len)`.
- `fn get<R>(self, r: R) -> Hash61` — \(O(1)\); The hash of a range of positions (`l..r`, `l..=r`, `..k`, `k..`, or a `Range<D>` when built over a `[D]T`); an empty range hashes to `Hash61(0)`.; traps: when the range reaches outside the hashed sequence
- `fn combine(self, a: Hash61, b: Hash61, b_len: Int) -> Hash61` — \(O(1)\) amortized (the power table grows past `len` on demand); The hash of `a`'s sequence followed by `b`'s, where `b` has length `b_len`: `a * base^b_len + b` modulo `2^61 - 1`.; traps: when `b_len < 0`
- `fn push<T: Hashable>(mut self, x: T)` — \(O(1)\) amortized; Appends `x` to the end of the hashed sequence.
- `fn pop(mut self)` — \(O(1)\); Removes the last element of the hashed sequence.; traps: when the hash is empty
- `fn lcp(self, a: Int, b: Int, of: ?RollingHash61 = None) -> Int` — \(O(\log n)\); The length of the longest common prefix of the suffixes at `a` and `b`, by binary search on hashes; `of: other` puts `b` in `other`, built with the same bases.; traps: when `a` is outside `0..=self.len`, `b` outside `0..=` the len of `of` (or `self`), or
- `fn lcs(self, a: Int, b: Int) -> Int` — \(O(\log n)\); The length of the longest common suffix of the prefixes `s[..a]` and `s[..b]`, by binary search on hashes.; traps: when `a` or `b` is outside `0..=self.len`

- `fn new<S: Indexed>(seq: S, bases: ?(Int, Int) = None) -> DynamicHash<D>` — \(O(n)\); A double-modulus rolling hash of `seq` that supports point updates, kept forwards and backwards in a segment tree; call it as `DynamicHash(seq)`.; traps: when a given base is outside `2..M`
- `@get fn len(self) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); The number of hashed positions, `D.count`.
- `@get fn is_empty(self) -> Bool` — \(O(1)\); True when there are no positions.

## `struct SuffixAutomaton<A>`

\(O(n \cdot \lvert A \rvert)\) space, \(O(1)\) amortized push.

Fields: `alpha: Count`, `next: List<Slot>`, `links: List<Slot>`, `max_len: List<Count>`, `first_end: List<Slot>`, `prefix: List<Bool>`, `letters: List<?A>`.

- `fn new() -> SuffixAutomaton<A>` — \(O(\lvert A \rvert)\); An empty suffix automaton over the alphabet domain `A`: only the root state `0`.
- `fn of<S: Seq>(s: S) -> SuffixAutomaton<A>` — \(O(\lvert s \rvert \cdot \lvert A \rvert)\) memory, \(O(\lvert s \rvert)\) amortized time; The suffix automaton of `s`: `SuffixAutomaton<A>()` followed by `push` of each element.; traps: when an element of `s` is not in `A`
- `fn push(mut self, a: A)` — \(O(1)\) amortized (\(O(\lvert A \rvert)\) for a cloned state); Appends the letter `a` to the string the automaton recognises the substrings of.; traps: never (`a` is an `A`)
- `@get fn root(self) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); The root state, for the empty string: always `0`.
- `@get fn len(self) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); The number of states, the root included; at most `max(1, 2n - 1)`.
- `fn step(self, state: Int, a: A) -> ?Int` — \(O(1)\); The state reached from `state` by the letter `a`, or `None` when that extension is not a substring.; traps: when `state` is outside `0..self.len`
- `fn link(self, state: Int) -> ?Int` — \(O(1)\); The suffix link of `state`: the state of its longest suffix that lies in another state; `None` at the root.; traps: when `state` is outside `0..self.len`
- `fn longest(self, state: Int) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); The length of the longest substring in `state`; `0` at the root.; traps: when `state` is outside `0..self.len`
- `fn shortest(self, state: Int) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); The length of the shortest substring in `state`, `longest(link) + 1`; `0` at the root.; traps: when `state` is outside `0..self.len`
- `fn first_pos(self, state: Int) -> ?Int` — \(O(1)\); The 0-based position where the first occurrence of `state`'s substrings ends; `None` at the root, whose only substring is empty.; traps: when `state` is outside `0..self.len`
- `fn find<S: Seq>(self, word: S) -> ?Int` — \(O(\lvert \mathit{word} \rvert)\); The state holding `word`, or `None` when `word` is not a substring; the root for an empty `word`.; traps: when an element of `word` is not in `A`
- `fn contains<S: Seq>(self, word: S) -> Bool` — \(O(\lvert \mathit{word} \rvert)\); True when `word` is a substring of the automaton's string: `find(word) != None`.; traps: when an element of `word` is not in `A`
- `fn distinct(self) -> Int` — \(O(\mathit{states})\); The number of distinct non-empty substrings: the sum of `longest(v) - shortest(v) + 1` over the states other than the root.
- `fn topo_order(self) -> List<Int>` — \(O(\mathit{states})\); Every state, by non-decreasing `longest` (counting sort), so each state comes after its suffix link; iterate it backwards to push values up the links.
- `fn occ_counts(self) -> List<Int>` — \(O(\mathit{states})\); For each state, the number of end positions of its substrings in the automaton's string; the root counts every position, `n`.
- `fn lcs<S: Seq>(self, other: S) -> (len: Int, end: Int)` — \(O(\lvert \mathit{other} \rvert)\); A longest common substring of the automaton's string and `other`, as `(len, end)` with `other[end - len..end]` the substring (positions in `other`, from 0).; traps: when an element of `other` is not in `A`
- `fn reset(mut self)` — \(O(1)\); Moves the append point back to the root, so the next `push` starts a new word of a generalized automaton (the substrings of all words added so far).
- `fn add_word<S: Seq>(mut self, word: S)` — \(O(\lvert \mathit{word} \rvert)\) amortized; Adds `word` as a separate word of a generalized automaton: `reset()`, then `push` each letter.; traps: when an element of `word` is not in `A`
- `fn states(self) -> yields Int` — \(O(\mathit{states})\); Every state in the order of `topo_order`, lazily.
- `fn endpos_tree(self) -> List<List<Int>>` — \(O(\mathit{states})\); The suffix-link tree as child lists: entry `v` lists the states whose link is `v`.
- `fn kth_substring(self, k: Int, distinct: Bool = true) -> ?List<A>` — \(O(\mathit{states} \cdot \lvert A \rvert)\); The `k`-th (0-based) non-empty substring in lexicographic order, as its letters, or `None` when there are not that many.; traps: when `k < 0`

## `struct PalindromicTree<A>`

\(O(n \cdot \lvert A \rvert)\) space, \(O(1)\) amortized push.

Fields: `alpha: Count`, `next: List<Slot>`, `slink: List<Count>`, `plen: List<Slot>`, `diff_val: List<Count>`, `ser_link: List<Count>`, `cnt: List<Count>`, `chars: List<A>`, `last: Count`, `front: List<A>`, `first: Count`, `undo: List<Count>`, `made: List<Count>`, `firsts: List<Count>`, `barrier: Int`.

- `fn new() -> PalindromicTree<A>` — \(O(\lvert A \rvert)\); An empty palindromic tree over the alphabet domain `A`: just the odd root `0` and the even root `1`.
- `fn of<S: Seq>(s: S) -> PalindromicTree<A>` — \(O(\lvert s \rvert \cdot \lvert A \rvert)\) memory, \(O(\lvert s \rvert)\) amortized time; The palindromic tree of `s`: `PalindromicTree<A>()` followed by `push` of each element.; traps: when an element of `s` is not in `A`
- `fn push(mut self, a: A) -> Int` — \(O(1)\) amortized; Appends the letter `a` and returns the state of the longest palindromic suffix of the new string, creating it if it is new.; traps: never (`a` is an `A`)
- `fn at(self, i: Int) -> A` — \(O(1)\); The character at position `i` of the current string, counting from the front.; traps: unless `0 <= i` and `i` is less than the current string's length
- `@get fn len(self) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); The number of states, both roots included: `distinct + 2`.
- `@get fn distinct(self) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); The number of distinct non-empty palindromic substrings, `len - 2`; at most `n`.
- `fn pal_len(self, state: Int) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); The length of the palindrome of `state`: `-1` at the odd root, `0` at the even root.; traps: when `state` is outside `0..self.len`
- `fn link(self, state: Int) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); The state of the longest proper palindromic suffix of `state`'s palindrome.; traps: when `state` is outside `0..self.len`
- `fn step(self, state: Int, a: A) -> ?Int` — \(O(1)\); The state of `a + P + a` where `P` is `state`'s palindrome, or `None` when that is not in the tree.; traps: when `state` is outside `0..self.len`
- `fn diff(self, state: Int) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); The difference `pal_len(state) - pal_len(link(state))`, the period that groups palindromic suffixes into series; `0` at both roots.; traps: when `state` is outside `0..self.len`
- `fn series_link(self, state: Int) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); The nearest state up the suffix links whose `diff` differs from `state`'s: `link(state)` when the diffs differ, else `series_link(link(state))`.; traps: when `state` is outside `0..self.len`
- `fn occ_counts(self) -> List<Int>` — \(O(\mathit{states})\); For each state, how many times its palindrome occurs in the pushed string, overlaps included; `0` at both roots.
- `fn push_front(mut self, a: A) -> Int` — \(O(1)\) amortized; Prepends the letter `a` (a double-ended tree) and returns the state of the longest palindromic prefix of the new string, creating it if it is new.; traps: never (`a` is an `A`)
- `fn pop(mut self)` — \(O(1)\) amortized; Undoes the most recent `push` not yet undone, removing the state it created if any, so a DFS over a tree of strings can back out.; traps: when there is no `push` to undo
- `@get fn last_state(self) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); The state of the longest palindromic suffix of the current string; the even root `1` when the string is empty.
- `fn contains<S: Seq>(self, word: S) -> Bool` — \(O(\lvert \mathit{word} \rvert)\); True when `word` is a palindrome occurring in the pushed string, that is, a state of the tree.
- `fn min_palindrome_partition(self) -> List<Int>` — \(O(n \log n)\); `dp[i]` is the least number of palindromes the first `i` pushed letters split into, for `i in 0..=n`, by the series-link DP.

## `struct Trie<A>`

Dynamic trie over alphabet domain `A`.

Fields: `alpha: Count`, `next: List<Slot>`, `ends: List<Count>`, `pass: List<Count>`.

- `fn new() -> Trie<A>` — \(O(\lvert A \rvert)\); An empty trie over the alphabet domain `A`: one root node `0`, no words.
- `@get fn root(self) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); The root node, for the empty word: always `0`.
- `@get fn len(self) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); The number of nodes, the root included.
- `@get fn is_empty(self) -> Bool` — \(O(1)\); True when no words are stored (every count is zero), whatever nodes remain.
- `fn step(self, node: Int, a: A) -> ?Int` — \(O(1)\); The child of `node` along `a`, or `None` when it was never created.; traps: when `node` is outside `0..self.len`
- `fn find<S: Seq>(self, word: S) -> ?Int` — \(O(\lvert \mathit{word} \rvert)\); The node of `word`, or `None` when no stored word starts with `word` (`count_prefix(word) == 0`).
- `fn add<S: Seq>(mut self, word: S) -> Int` — \(O(\lvert \mathit{word} \rvert)\); Inserts one copy of `word` and returns its terminal node; `count(word)` and `count_prefix(p)` for every prefix `p` of `word` grow by one.
- `fn remove<S: Seq>(mut self, word: S) -> Bool` — \(O(\lvert \mathit{word} \rvert)\); Removes one copy of `word`, reversing one `add`, and returns `true`; returns `false` and changes nothing when `count(word) == 0`.
- `fn count<S: Seq>(self, word: S) -> Int` — \(O(\lvert \mathit{word} \rvert)\); The number of copies of exactly `word` stored.
- `fn count_prefix<S: Seq>(self, prefix: S) -> Int` — \(O(\lvert \mathit{prefix} \rvert)\); The number of stored words (with multiplicity) that start with `prefix`.
- `fn ends_at(self, node: Int) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); The number of stored words that end at `node`.; traps: when `node` is outside `0..self.len`
- `fn pass_at(self, node: Int) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); The number of stored words that pass through or end at `node`; at the root, all of them.; traps: when `node` is outside `0..self.len`
- `fn contains<S: Seq>(self, word: S) -> Bool` — \(O(\lvert \mathit{word} \rvert)\); True when at least one copy of exactly `word` is stored: `count(word) > 0`.
- `fn clear(mut self)` — \(O(1)\); Removes every word and node, leaving just the root.
- `fn kth(self, k: Int) -> ?List<A>` — \(O(\mathit{depth} \cdot \lvert A \rvert)\); The `k`-th (0-based) stored word in lexicographic order, copies counted, as its letters; `None` when fewer than `k + 1` words are stored.; traps: when `k < 0`
- `fn count_less<S: Seq>(self, word: S) -> Int` — \(O(\lvert \mathit{word} \rvert \cdot \lvert A \rvert)\); The number of stored words (with multiplicity) lexicographically smaller than `word`.

## `struct AhoCorasick<A>`

\(O(\mathit{total} \cdot \lvert A \rvert)\) build, \(O(1)\) step.

Fields: `alpha: Count`, `goto: List<Slot>`, `fail: List<Count>`, `ends: List<List<Count>>`, `exit: List<Slot>`, `order: List<Count>`, `lens: List<Count>`, `pat_state: List<Count>`.

- `fn new<S: Seq>(patterns: List<S>) -> AhoCorasick<A>` — \(O(\mathit{sum} \lvert p \rvert \cdot \lvert A \rvert)\); The Aho-Corasick automaton of `patterns`; call it as `AhoCorasick<A>(patterns)`.; traps: when an element of a pattern is not in `A`
- `@get fn root(self) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); The root state, before any letter is read: always `0`.
- `@get fn len(self) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); The number of states, the root included.
- `fn step(self, state: Int, a: A) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); The state after reading `a` in `state`: the longest pattern prefix that is a suffix of what has been read.; traps: when `state` is outside `0..self.len`
- `fn link(self, state: Int) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); The failure link of `state`: the state of its longest proper suffix that is a pattern prefix; `0` at the root.; traps: when `state` is outside `0..self.len`
- `fn hit(self, state: Int) -> Bool` — \(O(1)\); True when some pattern ends at `state` itself or at a state up its failure links: `words_at(state)` is non-empty.; traps: when `state` is outside `0..self.len`
- `fn words_at(self, state: Int) -> List<Int>` — \(O(\mathit{output})\); Every pattern that ends at `state` or up its failure links, by index.; traps: when `state` is outside `0..self.len`
- `fn find_all<S: Seq>(self, text: S) -> yields (at: Int, pattern: Int)` — \(O(\lvert \mathit{text} \rvert + \mathit{output})\); Every occurrence of every pattern in `text`, as `(at, pattern)` with `at` the 0-based start: exactly the pairs with `text[at..at + patterns[pattern].len] == patterns[pattern]`.; traps: when an element of `text` is not in `A`
- `fn counts<S: Seq>(self, text: S) -> List<Int>` — \(O(\lvert \mathit{text} \rvert + \mathit{states})\); For each pattern, how many times it occurs in `text`, overlaps included: the number of `find_all` pairs with that index.; traps: when an element of `text` is not in `A`
- `fn fail_order(self) -> List<Int>` — \(O(\mathit{states})\); Every state in BFS order of the trie (root first, then by depth, equal depths by state number), so each state comes after its failure link; iterate backwards for bottom-up DP.
- `fn exit_link(self, state: Int) -> ?Int` — \(O(1)\); The nearest state strictly up the failure links of `state` at which a pattern ends, or `None` when there is None.; traps: when `state` is outside `0..self.len`
- `fn pattern_state(self, pattern: Int) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); The state where `patterns[pattern]` ends.; traps: when `pattern` is outside `0..patterns.len`

## `struct DynamicAhoCorasick<A>`

\(O(\lvert \mathit{pat} \rvert \cdot \lvert A \rvert \cdot \log n)\) amortized insert/delete, \(O(\lvert \mathit{text} \rvert \cdot \log n)\) query.

Fields: `alpha: Count`, `stored: Trie<A>`, `added: AcBuckets<A>`, `removed: AcBuckets<A>`.

- `fn new() -> DynamicAhoCorasick<A>` — \(O(1)\); An empty online pattern set over the alphabet domain `A`; call it as `DynamicAhoCorasick<A>()`.
- `@get fn len(self) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); The number of patterns stored, copies counted.
- `@get fn is_empty(self) -> Bool` — \(O(1)\); True when no patterns are stored.
- `fn add<S: Seq>(mut self, pattern: S)` — \(O(\lvert \mathit{pattern} \rvert \cdot \lvert A \rvert \cdot \log n)\) amortized; Stores one more copy of `pattern`.; traps: when an element of `pattern` is not in `A`
- `fn remove<S: Seq>(mut self, pattern: S)` — \(O(\lvert \mathit{pattern} \rvert \cdot \lvert A \rvert \cdot \log n)\) amortized; Removes one stored copy of `pattern`.; traps: when no copy of `pattern` is stored
- `fn count_matches<S: Seq>(self, text: S) -> Int` — \(O(\lvert \mathit{text} \rvert \cdot \log n)\); The total number of occurrences of all stored patterns in `text`, overlaps and copies counted.; traps: when an element of `text` is not in `A`

## Functions

- `fn repeat(self: Str, n: Int) -> Str` — \(O(\lvert \mathit{self} \rvert \cdot n)\); `self` written `n` times in a row, as a new `Str`: `"0".repeat(4)` is `"0000"`.; traps: when `n < 0`
- `fn starts_with<S: Indexed, P: Indexed>(self: S, pat: P, at: Int = 0) -> Bool` — \(O(\min(\lvert \mathit{self} \rvert - \mathit{at}, \lvert \mathit{pat} \rvert))\); True when `pat` occurs in `self` starting at position `at` (default 0, so a prefix test): the `pat.len` elements of `self` from `at` equal those of `pat` in order, `false` when they run past the end.; traps: when `at` is outside `0..=self.len`
- `fn ends_with<S: Indexed, P: Indexed>(self: S, pat: P) -> Bool` — \(O(\min(\lvert \mathit{self} \rvert, \lvert \mathit{pat} \rvert))\); True when `self` closes with `pat`: the last `pat.len` elements of `self` equal those of `pat` in order.
- `fn search<S: Indexed<K, T>, K, T, P>(self: S, p: P) -> ?K` — \(O(\lvert \mathit{self} \rvert + \lvert p \rvert)\); The key where `p` first stands in `self`, or `None`.
- `fn rsearch<S: Indexed<K, T>, K, T, P>(self: S, p: P) -> ?K` — \(O(\lvert \mathit{self} \rvert + \lvert p \rvert)\); The key where `p` last starts in `self`, or `None`.
- `@get fn lower(self: Char) -> Char` — \(O(1)\); The lowercase letter of an ASCII capital; any other character is returned as it is.
- `@get fn upper(self: Char) -> Char` — \(O(1)\); The capital of an ASCII lowercase letter; any other character is returned as it is.
- `@get fn digit(self: Char) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); The value `0..=9` of an ASCII decimal digit: `'7'.digit` is `7`.; traps: when `self` is not in `'0'..='9'` (test with `is_digit` first)
- `@get fn is_digit(self: Char) -> Bool` — \(O(1)\); True when `self` is an ASCII decimal digit, `'0'..='9'`.
- `@get fn is_lower(self: Char) -> Bool` — \(O(1)\); True when `self` is an ASCII lowercase letter, `'a'..='z'`.
- `@get fn is_upper(self: Char) -> Bool` — \(O(1)\); True when `self` is an ASCII capital letter, `'A'..='Z'`.
- `@get fn is_alpha(self: Char) -> Bool` — \(O(1)\); True when `self` is an ASCII letter, `'a'..='z'` or `'A'..='Z'`.
- `@get fn is_alnum(self: Char) -> Bool` — \(O(1)\); True when `self` is an ASCII letter or decimal digit.
- `@get fn is_space(self: Char) -> Bool` — \(O(1)\); True when `self` is one of the four ASCII whitespace characters `' '`, `'\t'`, `'\n'`, `'\r'`.
- `fn to_lower(self: Str) -> Str` — \(O(\lvert \mathit{self} \rvert)\); A copy of `self` with every ASCII capital replaced by its lowercase letter (`Char.lower`).
- `fn to_upper(self: Str) -> Str` — \(O(\lvert \mathit{self} \rvert)\); A copy of `self` with every ASCII lowercase letter replaced by its capital (`Char.upper`).
- `fn trim(self: Str) -> Str` — \(O(\lvert \mathit{self} \rvert)\); A copy of `self` with leading and trailing whitespace (`Char.is_space`) removed; inner whitespace is kept.
- `fn trim_start(self: Str) -> Str` — \(O(\lvert \mathit{self} \rvert)\); A copy of `self` with leading whitespace (`Char.is_space`) removed.
- `fn trim_end(self: Str) -> Str` — \(O(\lvert \mathit{self} \rvert)\); A copy of `self` with trailing whitespace (`Char.is_space`) removed.
- `fn split_once(self: Str, sep: Char) -> ?(Str, Str)` — \(O(\lvert \mathit{self} \rvert)\); `self` cut at the first `sep` into `(before, after)`, neither holding that `sep`; `None` when `sep` does not occur.
- `fn split_whitespace(self: Str) -> List<Str>` — \(O(\lvert \mathit{self} \rvert)\); The maximal runs of non-whitespace characters of `self` (`Char.is_space` separates), as new strings.
- `fn join<S: Seq>(self: Str, parts: S) -> Str` — \(O(\text{total output length})\); The elements of `parts` in order with `self` between each adjacent pair: `", ".join(xs)`.
- `fn replace(self: Str, from: Str, to: Str) -> Str` — \(O(\lvert \mathit{self} \rvert + \lvert \mathit{output} \rvert)\); A copy of `self` with every occurrence of `from` replaced by `to`.; traps: when `from` is empty
- `fn parse_int(self: Str, base: Int = 10) -> ?Int` — \(O(\lvert \mathit{self} \rvert)\); `self` read as a signed integer in `base`, or `None` if malformed or out of `Int` range.; traps: when `base` is outside `2..=36`
- `fn parse<T: Read>(self: Str) -> ?T` — \(O(\lvert \mathit{self} \rvert)\); `self` read as a `T` by the same rules as `read<T>()` (core 10.2), or `None` if a token is malformed, out of `T`'s range, missing, or left over.
- `fn z_function<S: Indexed<K, T>, K, T: Eq>(s: S) -> [K]Int` — \(O(n)\); The Z-array of `s`: `z[i]` is the length of the longest common prefix of `s` and the suffix starting at `i`; `z` at the first key is `s.len`.
- `fn prefix_function<S: Indexed<K, T>, K, T: Eq>(s: S) -> [K]Int` — \(O(n)\); The prefix function (failure function) of `s`: `p[i]` is the length of the longest proper prefix of `s` up to and including `i` that is also a suffix of it.
- `fn find_all<S: Indexed<K, T>, P: Indexed<L, T>, K, L, T: Eq>(self: S, pat: P) -> yields K` — \(O(\lvert \mathit{self} \rvert + \lvert \mathit{pat} \rvert)\); The start key of every occurrence of `pat` in `self`, overlapping ones included (Knuth-Morris-Pratt).
- `fn common_prefix_len<A: Indexed, B: Seq>(self: A, other: B) -> Int` — \(O(\min(\lvert \mathit{self} \rvert, \lvert \mathit{other} \rvert))\); The length of the longest common prefix of `self` and `other`, comparing values in order from the first key of each.
- `fn common_suffix_len<A: Indexed, B: Indexed>(self: A, other: B) -> Int` — \(O(\min(\lvert \mathit{self} \rvert, \lvert \mathit{other} \rvert))\); The length of the longest common suffix of `self` and `other`, comparing values in order from the last key of each.
- `fn period<S: Indexed>(s: S) -> Int` — \(O(n)\); The shortest period of `s`: the smallest `d >= 1` with `s[i] == s[i + d]` wherever both sides exist.
- `fn is_palindrome<S: Indexed>(s: S) -> Bool` — \(O(n)\); True when `s` reads the same forwards and backwards.
- `fn borders<S: Indexed>(s: S) -> yields Int` — \(O(n)\); The length of every non-empty proper border of `s` (a prefix that is also a suffix, shorter than `s`).
- `fn prefix_matches<S: Indexed<K, T>, P: Indexed<J, T>, K, J, T: Eq>(self: S, pat: P) -> [K]Int` — \(O(\lvert \mathit{self} \rvert + \lvert \mathit{pat} \rvert)\); For each key `i` of `self`, the length of the longest prefix of `pat` that ends at `i` (the KMP matcher's state after reading `self[i]`).
- `fn overlap<A: Indexed, B: Indexed>(a: A, b: B) -> Int` — \(O(\lvert a \rvert + \lvert b \rvert)\); The length of the longest suffix of `a` that is also a prefix of `b`, at most `min(\|a\|, \|b\|)`; how far `b` can slide onto the end of `a`.
- `fn lyndon_factorization<S: Indexed<K, T>, K, T>(s: S) -> List<K>` — \(O(n)\); The start key of each factor of the Lyndon factorization of `s` (Duval): the unique way to cut `s` into Lyndon words `w1 >= w2 >= ...` in lexicographic order.
- `fn min_rotation<S: Indexed<K, T>, K, T>(s: S) -> ?K` — \(O(n)\); The key at which the lexicographically smallest cyclic rotation of `s` starts (Booth).
- `fn max_rotation<S: Indexed<K, T>, K, T>(s: S) -> ?K` — \(O(n)\); The key at which the lexicographically greatest cyclic rotation of `s` starts.
- `fn shift_and<S: Indexed<K, T>, P: Indexed<L, T>, K, L, T: Eq>(self: S, pat: P) -> yields K` — \(O(\lvert \mathit{self} \rvert \cdot \mathit{ceil}(\lvert \mathit{pat} \rvert / 64))\); The start position of every occurrence of `pat` in `self`, overlapping ones included, by bit-parallel Shift-And.
- `fn find_all_wildcard<S: Indexed<K, Char>, P: Indexed<L, Char>, K, L>(self: S, pat: P, wildcard: Char = '?') -> yields K` — \(O(\lvert \mathit{self} \rvert \cdot \lvert \mathit{pat} \rvert)\) worst case, comparing directly; The start key of every place where `pat` matches `self` when each `wildcard` in `pat` matches any one element.
- `fn manacher<S: Indexed>(s: S) -> Palindromes` — \(O(n)\); The palindrome radii of `s` by Manacher's algorithm: `odd[i]` is the largest `k` with `s[i - k + 1..i + k]` a palindrome, and `even[i]` the largest `k` with `s[i - k..i + k]` one.
- `fn suffix_array<S: Indexed<K, T>, K, T: Ord>(s: S) -> SuffixArray<T>` — \(O(n)\) for `Str` and small integer alphabets, \(O(n \log n)\) otherwise; The suffix array of `s`; the same as `SuffixArray(s)`.
- `fn suffix_tree_edges<S: Indexed>(s: S) -> List<SuffixTreeEdge>` — \(O(n)\); Every edge of the compressed suffix tree of `s` (built from the suffix array and LCP array), one `SuffixTreeEdge` per edge of non-zero length.
- `fn lyndon_runs<S: Indexed>(s: S) -> List<(l: Int, r: Int, period: Int)>` — \(O(n \log n)\) time and memory; Every run (maximal repetition) of `s`, by the Lyndon-runs theorem: each `(l, r, period)` is a half-open range `s[l..r]` with smallest period `period`, `r - l >= 2 * period`, that cannot be extended left or right with the same period.
- `fn lcs_all<A, S: Seq>(words: List<S>) -> Int` — \(O(\mathit{sum} \lvert w \rvert \cdot \lvert A \rvert)\); The length of the longest sequence that is a substring of every word in `words`.
- `fn _gen_str(alphabet: Str, lo: Int, hi: Int) -> Str` — \(O(\mathit{hi})\); `gen<Str of alphabet>(len: lo..=hi)`.; traps: when `lo > hi` or `alphabet` is empty

## Example

```cp
print(z_function("ababa"))
// output: 5 0 3 0 1
```
